Subject: OSS threshold + UK nonresident — should we be charged VAT?

Hi Sean,

We're finalising our month-end accruals and a question came up from our tax team: BrightMarket sells a hosted analytics plugin to EU customers via our marketplace checkout. We are EU-established, but in June we sold several subscriptions to UK customers and the accounting team is unsure whether Redwood should be charging UK VAT on those invoices or whether the reverse charge applies (we're a UK nonresident for VAT purposes).

Specifics:
- Supply: digital SaaS (hosted inference) billed monthly from our platform in EUR.
- Buyer examples: UK-registered companies (B2B) and a few UK sole-traders.
- We completed OSS registration for EU B2C flows earlier this year but haven't added the UK.

Can you confirm Redwood's standard treatment for: (1) UK B2B customers with valid VAT IDs; (2) UK B2C customers where OSS doesn't cover the UK; and (3) any special invoice wording we should request to avoid misclassification?

Attaching a screenshot of our OSS registration screen and the tax team's sample invoice.

Thanks — appreciate a quick clarification.

Lucy
Finance Operations
BrightMarket

Attachments: BrightMarket-OSS-registration-screenshot.png; BrightMarket-vat-registration-form.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: OSS threshold + UK nonresident — should we be charged VAT?

Hi Lucy — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Marcus (tax lead) and Grace (billing ops) to provide definitive treatment and the exact invoice wording. High-level answers while they dig in: 

1) UK B2B with valid VAT ID: we generally do not charge UK VAT — reverse charge applies. We require a validated UK VAT number on file and will include the reverse-charge statement on the invoice.

2) UK B2C: if BrightMarket is nonresident for UK VAT and the sale is to a UK consumer, Redwood's position depends on whether BrightMarket has any UK VAT obligations; marketplace/OSS boundaries get tricky. If BrightMarket hasn't registered in the UK, we may need to charge VAT at UK rates for B2C sales or route through BrightMarket's OSS registration if applicable.

3) Invoice wording: we can add a standard clause for reverse-charge: "VAT reverse-charged under Article 194 (or relevant UK legislation) — recipient liable for VAT. Merchant VAT ID: [buyer VAT ID]." Marcus, can you confirm the precise phrasing we should use and whether we need to collect additional evidence (eg MOSS/OSS reference, proof of customer business status)? Grace, please advise operational steps to block invoice issuance until buyer VAT is validated.

Sean
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Lucy / team — quick tax note after reviewing the facts and UK guidance: 

- For B2B: if the purchaser provides a valid UK VAT registration number, the supply is outside Redwood's UK VAT scope and the reverse charge generally applies. Invoice should state: "Reverse charge — VAT liable by the recipient (UK VAT Act 1994 / VAT Notice 700). Buyer VAT: <number>". Keep validated VIES lookup screenshot or equivalent as evidence.

- For B2C: since BrightMarket is nonresident and you have not registered in the UK for VAT, the safe route is to charge UK VAT on B2C supplies. However, if BrightMarket wants Redwood to treat these as BrightMarket's OSS sales, BrightMarket must provide OSS registration details that specifically include UK liability (post-Brexit rules vary).

- Evidence & workflow: require the following to avoid charging VAT on B2B: VAT number + VIES validation or copy of certificate; billing address consistent with company registration; PO or purchase order where available. We should also record the invoice wording and a tax note in the invoice metadata.

Operational ask: Grace — please hold any invoices to UK customers flagged as business until we validate VAT numbers. If a VAT number fails VIES, we should run the buyer through a secondary validation (company registry) and flag for finance.

Marcus
Senior Tax Counsel
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — implementing the following ops changes today: 

- Flagging: add a "VAT validation required" flag to UK invoices created via marketplace when buyer country = UK and buyer type != consumer.
- Hold: any invoice with that flag will be held in the billing queue and not sent to customers until validation completes.
- Evidence capture: allow uploads to the invoice record (VIES screenshot, VAT certificate).
- Invoice wording template: will add Marcus's reverse-charge clause and a short footnote for B2C cases where we default to charging UK VAT.

Lucy — we'll need a list of the UK customers from June and July that were billed via your checkout so we can reconcile and reissue where necessary. Please send the list (company name, billing email, invoice numbers). I'll take ownership of reissue or credit notes as required.

Grace
